newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigeria says refineries fine despite fuel crunch.
newsitem.headline: Nigeria says refineries fine despite fuel crunch.

text.p: State-run Nigerian National Petroleum Corp (NNPC) said on Saturday that Nigerian refineries were operating normally despite a fuel shortage that has gripped the oil-producing nation.
"Refineries operation has nothing to do with the problem of product supply in Lagos," NNPC said in a statement.
Lagos, the biggest city, and several neighbouring areas are suffering a fuel shortage, the fifth this year in a perennial phenomenon in Africa's leading crude oil producer.

Local newspapers blame the latest shortage on the state of the refineries but also say vessels carrying fuel from the south-east could not dock in Lagos because their crew did not have proper immigration papers.
The NNPC statement said its refineries in Port Harcourt, Kaduna and Warri had been operating steadily for the past two to three weeks.

"Warri refinery particularly, this morning, actually commissioned an additional catalytic reforming unit that has been under rehabilitation since 1994," it said, adding "This has the effect of enhancing the refinery's petrol production."

"The only known and identified cause of the fuel shortage in Lagos and its environs is the activities of immigration personnel within the security task force at the product evacuation ports," the NNPC said.
Nigeria's four refineries have a theoretical capacity of 445,000 barrels per day but produce well below that.
The NNPC statement said Port Harcourt and Kaduna refineries were producing at 70 percent capacity and Warri at 60 percent. It was silent about the second refinery also located in Port Harcourt.
